source.title: Neural Symbolic Regression that Scales
source.authors: Luca Biggio; Tommaso Bendinelli; Alexander Neitz; Aurélien Lucchi; Giambattista Parascandolo

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports how symbolic-regression accuracy changes with pre-training dataset size, but it does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling, extrapolation of loss laws, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. It cites Kaplan et al. and says its accuracy trend is in accordance with that work.
record.gate_note: The paper's pre-training-data sweep measures symbolic-regression accuracy, not any claim version's named loss, allocation, architecture, modality-law, or downstream-language-model measure. Its own data-size result is recorded under fits_no_version. The paper also reports test-time compute and number-of-points results, which do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study varies pre-training dataset size for a 26M-parameter symbolic-regression Transformer and reports equation-recovery accuracy, not held-out loss. No power-law fit, no loss-vs-scale curve, no compute-optimal split and no shape sweep are reported. It cites Kaplan et al. only to say its accuracy trend is 'in accordance'. No version's named measure is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that NeSymReS accuracy steadily improves with pre-training dataset size and that the trend 'appears to continue for even larger datasets'. They also say it outperforms hand-designed baselines in time and accuracy. They describe their experiments as small-scale and suggest the method could improve with much larger compute.
record.recipe_differences: Different task and metric from the original language-model scaling studies; this paper trains a symbolic-regression system and evaluates equation-recovery accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported symbolic-regression accuracy changes with pre-training dataset size; test-time compute and the number of test input-output points are also varied in separate experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: NeSymReS out-of-distribution accuracy (A1ood, and A2ood in the appendix) rises from 10K to 10M pre-training equation skeletons on all five test sets. The test-time budget is fixed at about 100 s. Values are readable from figures only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a pre-trained symbolic-regression Transformer, downstream equation-recovery accuracy increases monotonically with synthetic pre-training dataset size over three orders of magnitude.

record.problems: The reported dataset-size trends are not fitted to a power law, and the numerical values are available only in plots. The paper describes the experiments as relatively small in model and dataset scale compared with the largest large-scale experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version result rows were omitted. Test-time compute and number-of-input-points findings are excluded because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute; only one model size is trained and loss is not plotted against dataset size.
Extrapolation of fitted power laws; none fitted.
Depth/width effects at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in a non-text regime; the symbolic-regression setting is reported only as monotone accuracy gains, with no power-law fit.
Downstream predictability from scale or loss. Accuracy rises monotonically with data, but no predictive relation is fitted.
Dependence of exponents or allocation on setup or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly unlinked (versions none). The model size is stated inconsistently in the paper: 11M+13M in the main text, 11M+15M in the appendix, and '26-million parameters' elsewhere. All dataset-size models were trained for the same number of iterations with early stopping, so data size is confounded with repetition and early stopping. The Figure 6 training curve is for the main model only and gives no scaling evidence. The text says 'In Figure 7' for the A1 results, but the A1 results are in Figure 2 and Figure 7 shows A2.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs' loss from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token counts as functions of training compute.
Effect of depth, width, or other architecture details on loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the study reports symbolic-regression accuracy, not a power-law fit to loss.
Predictability of downstream language-task performance from scale or pre-training loss.
Dependence of language-model loss exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: NeSymReS
rows.operation_detail: Varied the pre-training dataset size; reported out-of-distribution accuracy at a fixed test-time compute budget.
rows.value: Accuracy increases as the pre-training dataset size increases from 10K to 10M; numerical values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the mean estimate is used for plot error bars; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text explicitly reports the increasing trend for all five test sets; the numerical curve values are shown only in the figure.
